entries.test: The Remote Labor Index's published results, task selection, and exclusion criteria would establish the reported percentage and whether excluding physical labor inflated its applicability to human tasks overall.
entries.note: Marcus endorses this interpretation of the study; faithful extraction does not establish that his interpretation is accurate.
“May well” explicitly hedges the claim. In context, it concerns reassessing economic impact already attributed to AI, without specifying a future outcome.

entries.test: Public research on generative AI's effects on educational outcomes and information integrity, together with measurements of AI-generated nonconsensual pornography, would test the asserted widespread harms.
entries.note: The wording is emphatic, but it commits to substantial existing harms and widespread production of nonconsensual pornography.

entries.test: Public environmental assessments of AI data centers, alongside construction, utilization, and demand projections, would test environmental risks and whether expansion exceeds substantiated demand.
entries.note: “Too much speculation” is imprecise, but the sentence has a plain empirical core concerning environmental risks from speculative data-center expansion.

entries.test: Trump's subsequent public statements and policy actions would establish whether he abandons his public backing of AI.
entries.note: The metaphor forecasts disengagement, but the normalization makes its form more definite by specifying withdrawal of support. No deadline is stated.
